author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Apollo Global Management is in discussions to acquire Johnson & Johnson’s DePuy Synthes orthopedics business in a transaction that could value the unit near $20 billion, according to a Bloomberg report carried by Reuters. The talks could produce an agreement within weeks, but the process remains unsettled and other private-equity firms have also shown interest.

Johnson & Johnson may still choose a public separation instead of a sale. The company previously said it expected the orthopedics operation to become independent over an 18- to 24-month period. DePuy Synthes makes joint implants and surgical devices and generated about $9.3 billion in 2025 revenue, giving any transaction substantial scale within the medical-device sector.

Reuters said it could not independently verify the talks, and Apollo and Johnson & Johnson did not immediately respond to requests for comment. That makes the reported valuation and timing provisional. A sale would give Apollo a large established healthcare platform, while a spinoff could let public investors value the operation separately from J&J’s pharmaceutical and other device businesses. The unit has also faced litigation concerning some hip products.
dek: The private-equity firm is said to be in talks for DePuy Synthes, though Johnson & Johnson could still pursue a public separation instead.
headline: Report: Apollo explores deal for J&J orthopedics unit near $20 billion
